title: Fixture paper: every type
intro: One question of every kind. Sit it in one go, then read every reason.

stimuli.title: Kaveri Textiles
stimuli.text:
Kaveri Textiles Pvt Ltd sold 18% more cloth this year than last year. To win new dealers, it gave them 90 days to pay instead of 45.

Its bank balance at the year-end was the lowest in five years, and the finance team has asked two dealers to clear their overdue bills.

stimuli.title: How a ₹40 lakh budget is spent
Five interns in a row
stimuli.text:
Five interns, Asha, Bhavin, Chitra, Esha and Farhan, sit in a row facing north.
1. Chitra sits in the middle.
2. Farhan sits at the right end.
3. Asha sits immediately to the left of Chitra.
4. Esha does not sit next to Farhan.

options.text: The bundle of signed vouchers is on your desk.
The bundle of signed vouchers are on your desk.
The bundles of signed voucher is on your desk.
The bundle of signed vouchers were on your desk.

questions.reason: The subject is ‘bundle’, which is singular, so the verb is ‘is’. ‘Of signed vouchers’ only describes the bundle.

questions.stem: What best explains the fall in the bank balance?

options.text: The company sold less cloth this year.
The finance team stopped chasing overdue bills.
Dealers now take longer to pay for what they buy.
Dealers returned most of the extra cloth.

questions.reason: Sales rose, but dealers now get 90 days instead of 45, so more money is still with them. ‘Sold less’ contradicts the passage.

questions.stem: Which statement can you conclude from the passage?

options.text: The company’s profit fell this year.
Some dealers have not paid on time.
The company will cut the credit period next year.

questions.reason: The finance team is chasing two dealers for overdue bills. Profit and next year’s policy are not mentioned.
‘Criterion’ is singular; its plural is ‘criteria’, never ‘criterions’.

questions.stem: Listen and type the sentence exactly as you hear it.
questions.say: Please send the signed bank statement before the review meeting.

answer.text: Please send the signed bank statement before the review meeting.

questions.reason: Every word counts. Listen for the small words, such as ‘the’ and ‘before’.

questions.stem: Listen to the question, then answer it aloud in about 40 seconds.
questions.say: Tell me about a time you had to finish work under a tight deadline.

answer.model: During my Inter preparation, our college fest ended two weeks before my exams. As treasurer, I had three days to close the fest accounts. I listed every bill, chased the four vendors who had not sent invoices and finished the statement a day early. The teacher in charge used my sheet for the audit. I learnt to break a deadline into daily targets.
checklist: You answered the question that was asked
You said what you did and how it ended
You spoke for about 40 seconds without long pauses

questions.reason: A strong answer gives one real example: the deadline, what you did, and the result.

questions.stem: Your senior wants the bank reconciliation by 4 pm, but the March bank statement has not reached you. Write a short email to your senior in 60 to 80 words.

answer.model:
Subject: March bank reconciliation: statement awaited

Dear Rohan Sir,

The March bank statement for Kaveri Textiles has not reached me yet, so I cannot finish the reconciliation by 4 pm. I have matched every entry up to 28 February and listed the March cheques from the cash book. I have asked the client’s accountant to email the statement today. Once it arrives, I can send you the reconciliation within two hours.

Regards,
Neha
checklist: The subject line says what the mail is about
The first line states the problem
You say what you have done and what you need
A polite close with your name

questions.reason: Senior readers want the problem, what you have done and the new time, in that order.

questions.stem: A laptop listed at ₹60,000 is sold at a 15% discount, and then a further 5% off the discounted price. How much does the buyer pay?
questions.reason: Successive discounts multiply. Adding them to 20% gives ₹48,000, which is the trap.

questions.stem: In which month were net sales (sales minus returns) the highest?
questions.working: Net sales: April 39, May 36, June 45, July 43 (₹ lakh).
questions.reason: June has the highest net sales, ₹45 lakh, even after the largest returns.

questions.stem: Which team’s fees grew the fastest in percentage terms?
questions.working: Audit: 12 ÷ 120 = 10%. Tax: 12 ÷ 80 = 15%. Advisory fell by 5 ÷ 45, about 11%.
questions.reason: Audit and Tax both grew by ₹12 lakh, but Tax grew from a smaller base, so its rate is higher.

questions.stem: In how many months did the cash balance fall compared with the month before?
questions.working: Falls: February (24 to 18) and April (21 to 15). March, May and June rose.
questions.reason: Only February and April are lower than the month before.

questions.stem: What percentage of the budget goes on rent?
questions.reason: Share = part ÷ whole × 100, using the ₹40 lakh total.

questions.working: From the left: Chitra is 3rd, Farhan 5th, Asha 2nd. Esha cannot be 4th (next to Farhan), so Esha is 1st and Bhavin 4th.
questions.reason: Bhavin is 4th, next to Farhan. Esha is ruled out by clue 4.

questions.stem:
What is the price of one pen?
I. Three pens and two pencils together cost ₹50.
II. One pen costs ₹10 more than one pencil.

options.text: Either I or II alone is enough
I and II together are enough, but neither alone
Even I and II together are not enough

questions.working: Together: 3(q + 10) + 2q = 50, so q = ₹4 and a pen costs ₹14. Each statement alone has two unknowns.
questions.reason: Each statement alone leaves two unknowns; together they fix both prices.

questions.stem:
All audit files are in the cupboard. Some files in the cupboard are tax files.
Is this conclusion true: “Some audit files are tax files”?
questions.reason: The tax files in the cupboard may or may not be audit files, so the statements neither prove nor rule out the conclusion.

questions.stem: While vouching, you find a ₹48,000 purchase bill with no approval signature. What should you do first?

options.text: Sign the bill yourself so the file is complete before the review.
Ignore it, because ₹48,000 is below the materiality you were told.
Ask the client’s accountant to sign it as the approver today.
Note it as an exception in your working paper and tell your senior.

questions.reason: A missing approval is an exception to record and report. Signing it yourself or getting a back-dated signature hides the gap.

questions.stem: On 20 December 2025 a company pays ₹1,20,000 for a one-year insurance policy from 1 January 2026. Its books close on 31 March 2026. How much is prepaid on that date?
questions.reason: Prepaid is the unexpired part, 9 of 12 months. ₹30,000 is the part already used up.
